activities.name: Gather applicant personal and financial information

activities.name: Validate data completeness and format

activities.name: Score validation and exception handling

activities.name: Decision communication

activities.name: Campaign brief creation

activities.name: Creative asset production
activities.description: Design and produce digital assets (email templates, banners, social posts) and copy per channel

activities.name: Campaign setup and launch
activities.description: Configure audience lists, schedule sends, set budgets, and activate tracking across email, social, display, and SMS platforms

activities.name: Performance monitoring and lead qualification

activities.name: Review compliance alerts and approve account

activities.name: Provision account and deliver credentials

activities.name: Program Design

activities.name: Customer Enrollment

activities.name: Transaction Tracking

activities.name: Rewards Redemption Management

activities.name: Collect interaction data

activities.name: Segment customers

activities.name: Generate personalized content

activities.name: Monitor churn signals

activities.name: Segment Identification

activities.name: Feature Specification

activities.name: Compliance Validation

activities.name: Business Case Development

activities.name: Data aggregation

activities.name: Model calibration

activities.name: Decision approval

ai_opportunities.summary: Use NLP to auto‑extract personal and financial data from applicant forms or interview transcripts
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Document parsing and data extraction (NLP)
ai_opportunities.benefit: Reduces manual entry time by ~60% and lowers transcription errors
ai_opportunities.risk: Potential privacy breaches and mis‑extraction of critical fields
ai_opportunities.rationale: Local research (score 0.49) shows NLP can reliably pull identity, income, employment, and credit data from structured/unstructured inputs, but regulatory compliance still requires human oversight.

ai_opportunities.summary: AI can auto‑extract and preliminarily verify uploaded documents (pay slips, tax returns, ID, statements) using OCR and rule‑based checks.
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Document OCR, data extraction, and automated compliance validation
ai_opportunities.benefit: Reduces processing time by 30‑50% and lowers manual entry errors
ai_opportunities.risk: Potential privacy breaches and false‑negative validation of legitimate documents
ai_opportunities.rationale: Local research (score 0.54) shows AI can reliably extract data from uploaded PDFs, but human oversight remains needed for compliance and edge cases.

ai_opportunities.summary: AI can automatically validate retail banking data completeness and format using learned validation rules
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Machine learning‑based data validation
ai_opportunities.benefit: Speeds processing and reduces manual errors
ai_opportunities.risk: False positives/negatives may cause unnecessary rework or missed issues
ai_opportunities.rationale: Evidence describes validation rules and constraints that can be encoded in ML models to check required fields and formats, enabling automated checks.

ai_opportunities.summary: Apply AI-driven automated risk assessment to pre‑screen eligibility using rule‑based and scoring models
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Automated risk scoring / rule‑based decision engine
ai_opportunities.benefit: Real‑time, consistent eligibility decisions with higher throughput and compliance
ai_opportunities.risk: Potential bias in thresholds and regulatory scrutiny over automated credit decisions
ai_opportunities.rationale: Evidence shows automated risk assessment tools use AI and rule‑based systems to evaluate and score risks in real time, replacing slow manual reviews (evidence 0.54, 0.46)

ai_opportunities.summary: AI can automate data ingestion, cleaning, and normalization for loan applications in retail banking
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Data extraction, cleansing, and transformation using ML/NLP pipelines
ai_opportunities.benefit: Reduces processing time by up to 70% and improves data quality consistency
ai_opportunities.risk: Incorrect parsing of legacy formats or biased cleaning rules may lead to faulty credit decisions
ai_opportunities.rationale: Local research corpus indicates AI excels at structured financial data preprocessing, enabling high‑speed, repeatable pipelines

ai_opportunities.summary: Run predictive credit risk model on dataset to generate scores
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Predictive modeling and automated risk scoring
ai_opportunities.benefit: Real‑time, consistent credit risk scores with higher throughput
ai_opportunities.risk: Model bias or regulatory non‑compliance if inputs or logic are flawed
ai_opportunities.rationale: Evidence shows automated risk assessment tools use AI to evaluate and score risks in real time, replacing manual reviews (evidence 0.62, 0.61, 0.59).

ai_opportunities.summary: AI-driven anomaly detection and rule-based scoring can automatically validate model outputs and flag exceptions for review
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Anomaly detection with rule-based decision logic
ai_opportunities.benefit: Real‑time, consistent scoring reduces manual effort and speeds exception identification
ai_opportunities.risk: Potential false positives/negatives leading to missed risks or unnecessary escalations
ai_opportunities.rationale: Evidence shows automated risk assessment uses AI and configurable scoring matrices to evaluate outputs in real time, but human oversight remains needed for flagged anomalies (evidence 0.53, 0.50).

ai_opportunities.summary: Use AI-driven risk scoring to automatically record final underwriting scores and trigger decision notifications to loan officers or customers
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: AI risk scoring and rule-based workflow automation

ai_opportunities.risk: Potential mis‑scoring or rule mis‑configuration could lead to incorrect decisions and regulatory compliance issues
ai_opportunities.rationale: Evidence shows configurable AI risk scoring and automated rule‑based processes can record scores and notify stakeholders in real time (evidence 0.45, 0.46)

ai_opportunities.summary: AI can draft campaign briefs by extracting objectives, segments, messaging, and channels from existing data and templates
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Natural language generation and information extraction
ai_opportunities.benefit: Speeds brief creation, ensures consistency, and frees analysts for strategic refinement
ai_opportunities.risk: Potential omission of nuanced business context or regulatory constraints
ai_opportunities.rationale: Evidence shows AI can retrieve and synthesize corpus data to populate brief components, but human oversight remains needed for compliance

ai_opportunities.summary: Generative AI can draft copy and create digital design assets for emails, banners, and social posts, accelerating production while requiring human review for brand alignment
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Natural language generation and generative image/model creation
ai_opportunities.benefit: Reduces turnaround time and enables rapid personalization across channels
ai_opportunities.risk: Potential brand voice drift, regulatory compliance issues, and bias in generated content
ai_opportunities.rationale: Evidence shows AI can move concepts to engineered outputs (0.51) and that copywriting aims to persuade (0.40), indicating generative models fit the task but human oversight remains essential

ai_opportunities.summary: AI can auto-generate audience segments, budget allocations, and schedule sends using predictive models, while monitoring cross‑channel performance in real time
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Predictive audience modeling, budget optimization, multi‑channel scheduling, and automated tracking integration
ai_opportunities.benefit: Faster campaign launch, higher ROI through data‑driven audience selection and budget efficiency
ai_opportunities.risk: Model bias or data quality issues could mis‑target audiences, leading to wasted spend and compliance concerns

ai_opportunities.summary: Apply AI-driven real‑time scoring models to monitor performance metrics and qualify leads for sales handoff
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Predictive risk/lead scoring using attribution models

ai_opportunities.risk: Model bias or mis‑scoring could mis‑prioritize leads, leading to lost opportunities or compliance issues

ai_opportunities.summary: AI can automate data extraction and biometric verification in e‑KYC, speeding onboarding while ensuring compliance
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Computer vision for document and selfie verification, plus NLP for data validation
ai_opportunities.benefit: Reduces processing time and manual errors, improves fraud detection, and enhances customer experience
ai_opportunities.risk: Potential false‑rejects, bias in biometric models, and regulatory compliance concerns
ai_opportunities.rationale: Evidence shows eKYC relies on electronic data, biometric authentication and automated verification tools (e.g., document upload, live selfie) to create digital identity profiles, indicating AI‑driven verification can augment human review

ai_opportunities.summary: AI-driven eKYC for document capture, OCR, facial matching and compliance checks
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Computer Vision (OCR & facial recognition) + NLP for compliance rule checking
ai_opportunities.benefit: Speeds onboarding, cuts manual effort and fraud risk
ai_opportunities.risk: Potential false‑matches, bias, and regulatory compliance errors
ai_opportunities.rationale: Evidence shows eKYC uses OCR, selfie capture and AI fraud analysis to verify IDs and addresses, enabling fully automated digital onboarding (e.g., 0.52 evidence).

ai_opportunities.summary: AI can assist compliance officers by pre‑screening alerts and recommending approval decisions
ai_opportunities.ai_capability: AI‑driven risk assessment and decision support
ai_opportunities.benefit: Reduces review time and improves consistency of approvals
ai_opportunities.risk: Incorrect AI judgments could lead to regulatory breaches or missed fraud
ai_opportunities.rationale: Evidence shows AI tools can identify and prioritize risks in real‑time (0.52) and provide expert regulatory guidance (0.53), supporting but not replacing human final approval.

ai_opportunities.summary: AI can automate account creation, feature assignment, and digital welcome kit delivery in retail banking

ai_opportunities.ai_capability: Document OCR and facial recognition for identity verification
ai_opportunities.benefit: Speeds enrollment, reduces manual errors, and enhances fraud detection
ai_opportunities.risk: Data privacy concerns and potential bias in biometric matching
ai_opportunities.rationale: Evidence shows loyalty program management focuses on capturing personal information and improving retention, implying AI can augment data capture and verification (evidence 0.47, 0.48)

ai_opportunities.summary: AI can automatically record eligible transactions, compute loyalty points, and update balances instantly using real-time classification models

ai_opportunities.summary: AI can automate rewards redemption by applying business rules and loyalty program logic to process requests, apply discounts, and reconcile inventory

ai_opportunities.benefit: Near‑real‑time processing, reduced manual errors, and consistent compliance

ai_opportunities.summary: AI can parse regulatory texts and competitive data to suggest product features, pricing, and eligibility rules

sources.title: Predictive modelling
sources.raw_excerpt: In finance and mathematics, predictive modelling is the use of statistics to predict outcomes. Most often the event one wants to predict is in the future, but predictive modelling can be applied to any type of unknown event, regardless of when it occurred. For example, predictive models are often used to detect crimes and identify suspects, after the crime has taken place.The output of predictive models can come in multiple forms, such as an estimated probability of a certain event occurring (e.g. Binary regression), or a scalar response variable (e.g. Linear regression) The usage of predictive modelling in business decision making is often referred to as predictive analytics.Predictive modelling is often contrasted with causal modelling. In the former, one may be entirely satisfied to make use of indicators of, or proxies for, the outcome of interest. In the latter, one seeks to determine true cause-and-effect relationships. This distinction has given rise to a burgeoning literature in the fields of research methods and statistics and to the common statement that "correlation does not imply causation".Depending on definitional boundaries, predictive modelling is synonymous with, or largely overlapping with, the field of machine learning, as it is more commonly referred to in academic or research and development contexts. This growing field has been made more accessible through increases in computing power and new data architectures that allow for more efficient model training techniques (see Attention Is All You Need).As the power and complexity of predictive modelling continue to grow, fairness in predictive models has become a growing field of study, particularly given the applications of predictive modelling within areas such as healthcare, insurance, and lending.

sources.raw_excerpt: Data mining is the process of extracting and finding patterns in massive data sets involving methods at the intersection of machine learning, statistics, and database systems. Data mining is an interdisciplinary subfield of computer science and statistics with an overall goal of extracting information (with intelligent methods) from a data set and transforming the information into a comprehensible structure for further use. Data mining is the analysis step of the "knowledge discovery in databases" process, or KDD. Aside from the raw analysis step, it also involves database and data management aspects, data pre-processing, model and inference considerations, interestingness metrics, complexity considerations, post-processing of discovered structures, visualization, and online updating.The term "data mining" is a misnomer because the goal is the extraction of patterns and knowledge from large amounts of data, not the extraction (mining) of data itself. It also is a buzzword and is frequently applied to any form of large-scale data or information processing (collection, extraction, warehousing, analysis, and statistics) as well as any application of computer decision support systems, including artificial intelligence (e.g., machine learning) and business intelligence. Often the more general terms (large scale) data analysis and analytics—or, when referring to actual methods, artificial intelligence and machine learning—are more appropriate.The actual data mining task is the semi-automatic or automatic analysis of massive quantities of data to extract previously unknown, interesting patterns such as groups of data records (cluster analysis), unusual records (anomaly detection), and dependencies (association rule mining, sequential pattern mining).
